headline: Taiwan's president has urged Micron and its workers to negotiate in good faith to avoid a possible strike at the US memory chipmaker's Taiwan plants.
score_reason: Kept at pool score: a head of state steps into a possible strike at a key AI-memory site, but no strike has been called.
importance_line: It affects Micron's roughly 15,000 Taiwan workers and buyers of the memory used in AI servers, and no strike date has been set; the unions say the 19 Oct rally is not a strike.
summary: The Edge Malaysia reports that Taiwan's president Lai Ching-te, speaking on Thursday 15 Oct 2026 at the opening of a new Micron assembly and testing site in Taichung, urged Micron and its unions to negotiate "sincerely" after a union won member authorisation to strike over a bonus dispute. Micron's president and chief operating officer Manish Bhatia said the new factory's 2027 capacity is already sold out, and Micron employs about 15,000 people in Taiwan, its largest manufacturing hub.
notes: Original agency not named in the text.
